claims.text: The initial material is a homogenized, cast W–Nb–Mo–Ta refractory high-entropy alloy with a mean grain size of approximately 100 µm.
The intervention adds 0.5 at.% Hf to the W–Nb–Mo–Ta alloy.
The Hf-containing alloy is internally oxidized at 900 °C for 10 h in a controlled O₂ atmosphere.
The proposed treatment will precipitate HfO₂ particles with sizes of approximately 20–100 nm and a volume fraction of approximately 0.5%.
The resulting nanoscale HfO₂ dispersoids will be distributed throughout the alloy matrix.
HfO₂ dispersoids will impede dislocation motion through Orowan-type strengthening.
HfO₂ dispersoids will act as sinks for irradiation-generated point defects.
Point-defect absorption by the oxide particles will suppress irradiation-induced swelling.
The high-temperature stability of the oxide particles will preserve the alloy microstructure during thermal exposure.
The treatment will increase yield strength at 1000 °C by approximately 20% relative to the undoped alloy.
The treatment will reduce irradiation-induced swelling at 5 dpa by at least 10% relative to the undoped alloy.
The modified alloy will remain thermally stable up to 1200 °C.
The undoped W–Nb–Mo–Ta baseline alloy has a yield strength of approximately 350 MPa at 1000 °C.
The undoped W–Nb–Mo–Ta baseline alloy exhibits approximately 2% swelling at 5 dpa.
The predicted effects should hold for HfO₂ particle sizes of 20–100 nm and a volume fraction of approximately 0.5%.
The predicted irradiation response should hold at doses up to 5 dpa.
The predicted performance and stability should hold at testing or exposure temperatures up to 1200 °C.
